claims: Capability provider snapshot, invocation and scoped status operations return Promises. Host call context carries request/correlation, deadline, execution mode, cancellation and current-owner checks. A finite deadline bounds ignored cancellation; late results are withheld.

The resolver checks owner, snapshot scope/revision/expiry and invalidation epoch after awaits. Newer discovery supersedes older pending reads. Scope and execution mode bind cache use; replay discovery cannot become a live invocation. Cache expiry uses wall and monotonic time.

Status is read before consuming one-use admission. Actual admission receipts are passed to the provider. Arguments are copied before awaiting admission. Concurrent identical invocations share one attempt; changed arguments under the same identity are denied. Lost post-dispatch responses remain unknown and cannot trigger redispatch within the resolver. Durable cross-process idempotency remains the provider responsibility.

Skill execution awaits discovery and sequential invocation under its overall deadline, passes recorded step invocation identities, copies inputs and stops on uncertainty without retry or compensation.

Local HTTP tools await provider operations outside synchronous grant/review transactions. Current authentication, Assistant permission and grant state are checked while awaiting.
